newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two Spanish wineries to issues shares on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Two Spanish wineries to issues shares on bourse.

text.p: Two producers of Spanish Rioja wines said on Wednesday they would list shares on the bourse.
Compania Vinicola del Norte de Espana (CVNE), which produces the brands CVNE, Imperial and Vina Real, said it was planning a public share offering and a capital rise.

The group, which was founded in 1879 by the grandfather of the current chairman, said: "it has the intention of taking the necessary legal steps for a public share offering and a capital rise, offering the subscription rights publicly," CVNE said.
In addition, Spain's Baron de Ley said it would sell up to 74.6 percent of its share capital.

Baron de Ley is a private company, with a capital base of 4.85 billion pesetas, and its share sale will be directed at institutional investors, domestic and international investment funds, pension funds and portfolio listing.
Together with Bodegas and Bebidas, these two listings will bring the number of wineries on the Spanish bourse to three.
